Operator
If you would like to ask a question during this time, simply press star followed by the number one on your telephone keypad. If you would like to withdraw your question, press star one once again. Thank you. I would now like to turn the conference over to Daniel Jenkins, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.
Daniel Jenkins
Director of Investor Relations, Western Midstream Partners
Thank you. I'm glad you could join us today for Western Midstream conference call. I'd like to remind you of the accompanying slide deck and last night's earnings release disclosures regarding forward-looking statements and non-GAAP reconciliation.
Western Midstream's most recent Form 10-Q and other public filings for a description of risk factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from what we discussed today.
Relevant reference material. With me today are Michael J. Ure, our Chief Executive Officer, Kristen Shults, Craig Collins, our Chief Operating Officer. I'll now turn the call over to Michael.
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Thank you, Daniel. Good afternoon, everyone. Yesterday, we reported another expansion performance at Western Midstream. Our Q2 financial success was primarily driven by increased throughput across all three products in the Delaware Basin and higher distributions from equity investments. Partially offset gas throughput in the Delaware Basin of gas per day.
Record produced water throughput in the Delaware Basin, gathering 864,000 barrels per day and record adjusted EBITDA for the second straight quarter, generating substantial free cash flow. The return of capital to our stakeholders, specifically through July 29, we have repurchased approximately 7.1 million units in the open market and 10 million units from our million dollars of units at an average price of approximately $24.85 per unit.
Additionally, through our unit buyback programs and including the retired 59 million units, or approximately 13.2% of the unaffected common unit count, we also Senior notes during the quarter.
Inclusive of the previously mentioned unit repurchases, we have reduced our debt to trailing twelve months threshold of 3.4 times, and we have now retired just over $1.65 billion of Senior notes, or 20% of the aggregate debt balance since our January 2020 Senior notes issuance.
As of July 29, on a per unit basis, we have now returned $6.53 through debt retirement and unit repurchases, and $3.97 in distributions since our January 2020 Senior notes issuance, which excludes any market driven appreciation in our current unit price.
We are very pleased with our recent efforts to accelerate the return of capital to our stakeholders through debt retirement. Already below our year-end net leverage threshold of 3.4x gives us financial flexibility to evaluate other capital to our unitholders, whether it's distribution.
The decision to pay an enhanced distribution will be based on our financial performance in H2 2022. Additionally, with revolver borrowings, or if we refinance those borrowings with more permanent debt capital, those transactions would be excluded from the computation to potentially pay an enhanced distribution.
We only intend for permanent reductions in outstanding debt and equity in the aggregate to be considered in the enhanced distribution calculation. Turning to ESG, we released our ESG report. The report details how we are working to focus on people and operate responsibly.
We are very proud of the unique culture we have built at Western Midstream.
Our people have worked tirelessly to focus on minimizing our environmental footprint and to work with others to find creative solutions to some of today's energy and climate challenges.
This approach to advancing energy and our expertise in handling and transporting natural gas are reasons why we feel we are playing a key role. Our balance sheet and our strong operational execution all give us confidence that WES is well positioned for continued success, even in light of the recent market volatility and economic concerns.
Over the past few years, the midstream sector's capacity, prudent capital allocation, and improving the health of its respective balance sheets. This discipline has made our sector increasingly more attractive to investors.
West has been a leader amongst our peers by being the first in the industry to focus on free cash flow, meaningfully de-risking the enterprise, and creating value for our unit holders through the return of capital, the asset dynamics, and to continue returning capital to our stakeholders. With that, I will now turn. Kristen?
Kristen Shults
SVP and CFO, Western Midstream Partners
Thank you, Michael, and good afternoon, everyone. During Q2, we generated net income available to limited and another record-breaking quarter of adjusted EBITDA that totals to 548 million. The sequential quarter increase in adjusted EBITDA was driven by increased adjusted gross margin, partially offset by increased operation and maintenance expense.
Our adjusted gross margin increased by approximately 51 million. From equity investments also increased on a sequential quarter basis, which we do not expect to reoccur in Q3. Additionally, our strong plant performance in the Delaware Basin resulted in incremental gross under our fixed recovery contracts.
Our operation and maintenance expense increased by approximately 39 million on a sequential quarter basis, primarily associated with higher utility expenses and. We expect O&M to further increase in Q3 as we perform expected plant maintenance and complete a one-time $10 million field level project to support our transformation efforts.
After Q3, we expect O&M expense to be more in line with our Q2 results. While utility costs should decrease as prices and usage declines during the winter months, we expect to incur additional surface use fees as our produced water throughput increases.
Turning to cash flow, our Q2 cash flow from operations totaled 467 million, which was a material increase compared to the prior quarter course of business.
Free cash flow totaled 372 million, and free cash flow after the increase totaled approximately 100 million. Finally, we recently declared a Q2 cash distribution of 0.50 per unit payable on August 12. Looking to the H2 of the year, we expect throughput to continue to increase throughout the year and into 2023 due to continued strong producer activities in the Delaware Basin.
We expect to experience slight compression in our natural gas adjusted gross margin per Mcf as we further utilize our resources. Despite the headwinds associated with expected lower distributions from equity investments and higher O&M expense, we remain comfortable with our previously announced 2022 guidance ranges for adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow.
Finally, our remaining capital budget focuses on the organic expansion of our existing asset base and the construction of Mentone Train III.
We can provide flow assurance for our customers' volumes in 2023 and beyond. In the meantime, we're utilizing excess capacity in the Delaware Basin through offload arrangements that will bridge us to the expected completion. Craig to discuss our operational performance. Craig?
Craig Collins
Senior Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Western Midstream Partners
Thank you, Kristen. On a sequential quarter basis, natural gas throughput increased by 5%. This increase was primarily driven by increased volumes in the Delaware Basin. Our crude oil and natural gas liquids throughput decreased by 1% compared to the prior quarter.
Expected declines in the DJ Basin and reduced liquid throughput from our equity investments were partially offset by increased throughput in the Delaware Basin. Produced water throughput increased by 15% compared to the prior quarter due to increased volumes at the DBM water system.
Our per Mcf adjusted gross margin for our natural gas assets increased by 0.02 compared to the prior quarter, primarily due to changes in our contract mix and increased throughput at our West Texas complex, which has a higher per Mcf margin as compared to our other natural gas assets.
In addition, continued strong plant performance coupled with higher commodity prices benefited our margin in Q2. Our per-barrel adjusted gross margin for our crude oil and natural gas liquids assets increased by 0.13 compared to the prior quarter.
This was primarily driven by higher margin as compared to our other crude oil and NGL assets, and higher distributions despite lower throughput from equity investments. Our per-barrel adjusted gross margin for our produced water assets decreased by 0.10 compared to the prior quarter, primarily due to decreased efficiency fees, and changes in our contract mix as throughput increased.
We expect that the anticipated increase in throughput in the Delaware Basin in H2 will be partially offset by expected volume declines in the DJ Basin.
Regardless, we're maintaining our previous 2022 throughput exit rate expectations of mid-single-digit percentage growth in natural gas volumes, low single-digit growth in crude oil and NGL volumes, and low twenties percentage growth in produced water volumes. In the Delaware, we expect 202 wells to come online in the basin during the H2 of this year, which is approximately 65% of the total 2022 expected well count.
In the DJ, we expect our natural gas decline rate to slow down as we enter into 2023 as legacy wells enter a more mature phase of the production type curve. Third-party online volumes continue to flow onto our system and through continued activity in the Watkins area of the basin.
From an oil standpoint, we would expect the current decline rates to continue until additional rigs return to the acreage we service.
We are also encouraged by some positive momentum in the permitting process with the COGCC, where optimism is growing as they gain clarity on the permit approval process. Finally, from a supply chain and inflation standpoint, prices for most parts, we will benefit from pre-ordering a large portion of the steel pipe needed for organic expansion and well connects.
We have seen price increases for steel and other major items such as chemicals and lubricants. Despite these recent challenges, we continue to actively manage our revised 2022 guidance from last quarter. I'll now turn the call back over to Michael.
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Thanks, Craig. We released our annual sustainability report this week. I will highlight a few of our achievements here, but I encourage you to take some time to read the report.
We are very proud of our accomplishments addressing ESG issues since becoming a standalone organization. This year these achievements include technologies to enhance leak detection efforts and expand electrical compression in the field.
The expansion of our boards, which include 56% of our senior leadership and 30% of other managers who are female, or racial or ethnic minorities.
An extremely successful first year of our volunteer program, which saw 62% of our employees volunteer in the community and donations to nearly 200 causes. For such a young organization, the heart of our people is such an awesome quality of ours, one of which I'm personally most proud.
Thank you to all of our dedicated employees who have played such an integral role in reducing emissions and giving back to the community. Our track record in under three years of operating as a standalone organization is further evidence of our commitment to.
Building on this momentum in the years ahead as we continue to advance energy by enhancing the sustainability of our operations. To recap, we're very confident that Wes's financial track record of prudent capital allocation, operational efficiency, and strong returns to unitholders.
I'm also proud to say that Wes has been a leader in one of the lowest debt-to-EBITDA leverage ratios and continues to be a leader in proportional debt reduction and total units repurchased since early 2020 relative to our publicly traded midstream peers.
We will post an updated slide deck which we believe will continue to demonstrate WES's with comparative leadership in these regards.
Thanks to the hard work of our employees and contractors, our operational and financial performance through H1 of the year has been excellent, and we look forward to what's ahead in H2 2022. With that, we'll open the line for questions.
Operator
At this time, I would like to remind everyone, in order to ask a question, press star then the number one on your telephone keypad. We'll pause for just a moment to compile the Q&A roster. Your first question comes from the line of Gabriel Moreen. Your line is open.
Gabriel Moreen
Managing Director, Mizuho Americas
Hey, good afternoon, everyone. I thought I'd follow Kristen. I have a follow-up question just in terms of the unit repurchases. It seems like you were pretty aggressive and opportunistic around Q2.
Can you just talk about kind of, I guess, what you feel like your gating factor is at this point? I think we're close to 3.2 on an LTM basis right now. I just want to confirm that you still, you feel you have room to be opportunistic for the rest of the year considering kind of where your leverage targets are right now.
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
We definitely will continue to utilize that program as we see opportunities to do so. You know, again, as we think about the leverage target as it relates to enhanced distribution, the construct for that was, you know, whether or not we had other opportunities to utilize that excess free cash flow and to try and do that in a prudent way.
We still have $ half a billion left, or a little over $ half a billion left in the buyback program, and if there's opportunities to do that, then we will intentionally utilize the buyback program in order to repurchase units, you know, opportunistically in that regard. We'd certainly like to be in a place to be able to pay an enhanced distribution.
If there are other opportunities, including other opportunities to buy back additional units, then we'll continue to utilize that program for sure.
Gabriel Moreen
Managing Director, Mizuho Americas
Thanks, Michael. Maybe I can ask a follow-up to that. I'm just curious to what extent, you know, getting to IG is quite a bit out of your control, but I'm just curious, from a capital return standpoint, how you balance those things.
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Yeah. As it relates to leverage, we're certainly from a metric standpoint well within the ranges that have been established from the agencies in order to be in investment-grade territory, with frankly a fair amount of leeway relative to the metrics provided.
You know, we would still have a comfort level to be able to do that from a rating agency perspective. You know, as you noted, the constraint from that standpoint isn't necessarily the metrics that we're currently working under. I don't know, Kristen, if there's anything else to add there.
Kristen Shults
SVP and CFO, Western Midstream Partners
No. I think just in general, the conversations we've had with the rating agencies have been really positive on where we put our balance sheet. I don't see anything changing in that regard either.
Gabriel Moreen
Managing Director, Mizuho Americas
Some of your O&M commentary, just trying to understand here exactly what is seasonal versus structural versus maybe inflationary, if that all makes sense. Maybe you can just kind of recap what you're seeing on O&M. It sounds like it's going a little bit higher, but it's scaling back also a little bit in Q2 and beyond.
Kristen Shults
SVP and CFO, Western Midstream Partners
That's right. Just to take a step back, our Q1 O&M was a little bit lower. There is some seasonality on the utility side. We use more from a utility perspective during the summer months. We've also seen increased pricing on the utility side, so that's coming out in the Q2, and we expect that to continue into the Q3 as well.
The Q2 is probably a better run rate going forward, with the exception that in the Q3, we're expecting to spend around $10 million on a field level project that's working with our transformation efforts, allowing us to be more efficient and proactive on the maintenance and repair side. Expect a little bit of an uptick in the Q3 and then returning back to the Q2 level when we get into Q4.
Gabriel Moreen
Managing Director, Mizuho Americas
Great. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Jeremy Tonet. Your line is open.
Jeremy Tonet
Executive Director, J.P. Morgan
Hi, good afternoon.
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Hey, Jeremy. How are you?
Jeremy Tonet
Executive Director, J.P. Morgan
Good. Good. Just wanted to slice the buyback question slightly differently if I could. I was just wondering, when you guys think about unit repurchases, is it more driven by kind of unit price at a point in time or balance sheet capacity or other considerations such as trying to maximize or hit a certain level of free cash flow return to unit holders?
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Jeremy, all of those factors come into consideration as we execute on the buyback program. You know, again, so when we talk about opportunistic, you know, those are definitely many of the factors that are under consideration.
Are we seeing weakness, you know, out there and you know, therefore seeing opportunity to be able to repurchase, you know, balance sheet, free cash flow, and ability to potentially pay an enhanced distribution. All of those certainly are factors. We definitely saw in Q2 and into Q3 a meaningful opportunity in that regard to be able to utilize that program.
Jeremy Tonet
Executive Director, J.P. Morgan
Got it. Thanks for that. I just want to touch base on the CCS side, and Occidental obviously has big plans there. I'm just wondering your thoughts if IRA you know kind of changes things a bit, and is there a role for West to play here alongside Occidental in these initiatives?
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Yeah, it's a great question. You know, is currently being proposed obviously does provide incremental opportunities for, you know, everyone out there and, you know, clearly a leader in that regard.
Our close relationship with them has resulted in, you know, frequent and active dialogue around ways that West would be able to participate. Got it. That's helpful. I'll leave it there. Thanks. Thanks, Jeremy.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Neil Mehta. Your line is open.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director, Goldman Sachs
Hi. Thanks for taking my question. Just wanted to bridge the guidance raise given on the last quarter and where we are now. Maybe what's changed regarding O&M versus when you put out the guidance in Q1, what was expected and what was unexpected going forward, you know, structural versus inflation.
Second, it was mentioned that the GMP rates will decline going forward as you use offtake agreements. Was that anticipated, and how long will that persist? Will it be till Mentone III comes online?
Kristen Shults
SVP and CFO, Western Midstream Partners
Yeah. A couple of pieces in there. When we announced it took into account everything that you're seeing in Q2, and then it's still we're maintaining the GMP rates that you're discussing, margin per unit. That's as expected and was part of that revised guidance and still holds true today.
The O&M expense and the uptake that we were seeing, that was also part of that and expected as well. I think most of what we were expecting from an inflation standpoint, you know, just activity standpoint, spending standpoint is right in line with what we're seeing actuals right now and when we're looking into H2 2022.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director, Goldman Sachs
Okay, great. As a follow-up, just with the activity from the E&Ps in the Delaware and the announcements of new processing capacity by your peers, are you looking past Mentone III?
When do you think you would need a new processing plant beyond that, given just the increasing volumes in the Delaware? On the other side, how do you see DJ volumes trending over the next year or so?
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Yeah, we are absolutely constantly monitoring, you know, growth in additional capacity necessary from our standpoint. You know, that went into consideration of authorizing the incremental capacity at Mentone last quarter. It's been, frankly, continues to be just as positive, if not stronger, in terms of expectations going forward.
You probably, you know, keyed on the announcement that Occidental Petroleum mentioned yesterday with regards to the Ecopetrol JV that will be transitioning onto West acreage. That will, you know, likely increase activity levels in a pretty meaningful way for us going into 2023 and beyond. You know, as we need to take into consideration as we look at, you know, potential incremental capacity.
As it sits right now, there's nothing that we look at and see would be required, you know, as we sit here today. Craig, I don't know if you want to reiterate the commentary on DJ as it relates to volumes or anything to add there on the capacity side.
Craig Collins
Senior Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Western Midstream Partners
Yeah, I mean, we obviously continue to have more than sufficient capacity in the DJ. We've done a really good job, I think, at bringing additional gas onto the system, both from producers as well as from some of our peers, and we'll continue to look for those opportunities.
You know, it's going to start to flatten out a lot more than where it's been just based on the, you know, where the production, the base production is on the type curves up there. You know, we see that starting to slow down in terms of the rate decline going forward, but still be on decline, and you know, continue to look for opportunities up there in the DJ.
Nothing further to add to Michael's comments on the Delaware. I think that summed it up well.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director, Goldman Sachs
Okay, great. Thank you very much.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Michael Cusimano Your line is open.
Michael Cusimano
Broker, FINRA
Hi. Good afternoon, everyone. How much of your margin goes through the cost of service adjustments at year-end? Maybe hoping, like, you can comment, 'cause we've gotten feedback where some investors assume all of your fee goes through that adjustment. I think you've broken it out somewhat before in the past.
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Yeah. We actually talk about the percentage of our contracts that are around the 1% gas, 96% oil and 100% water that, from that perspective.
We don't actually break out what proportion of that is cost of service versus a volume commitment. There is most definitely a portion of that that is fixed fee oriented, and not all is cost of service.
Michael Cusimano
Broker, FINRA
Got it. Okay. Does it depend by commodity? You know, rates every.
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
We do have cost of service contracts on all three commodities. Oil and water. Again, different proportions of each of those. There are cost.
Michael Cusimano
Broker, FINRA
Okay. To follow up on that, I believe into this year the DJ rates had some downward pressure because that, you know, may not materialize with some of the permit issues that Occidental Petroleum is going to. Is it wrong to think that DJ rates could possibly improve year-over-year with that not materializing?
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
It's too early to tell at this stage. It's a great question, but it's too early to tell what the potential impact on rates are going to be.
You know, as Craig mentioned in his prepared remarks, we're starting to feel a little bit more optimistic as to achieve permits and on, you know, what our rates will be, expectation of when and at what time and to what extent volumes would come through the system out in the DJ.
Michael Cusimano
Broker, FINRA
Okay.
Operator
There are no further questions at this time.
Oscar K. Brown
President and CEO, Western Midstream Partners
Thank you, everyone. Looking forward to the future. Appreciate your time.
Operator
This concludes today's conference call. You may now disconnect.
